text:
ben: heads-up, we just saw a customer report where a streaming request that hit a router failover got billed for the truncated portion twice.

jia: ugh. any pattern? routing change on reconnect?

ben: looks like: initial stream on node A -> toolcall triggered -> client reconnects to node B -> node B resumes with prefix replay but toolcall TTL already expired so node B issues a separate toolcall attempt and both attempts get provisionally charged.

sam: so double provisional charge then one gets cleared later? or both stick?

ben: in this case the UI showed provisional tokens for both, reconciliation removed node B's toolcall charge later, but customer saw the spike in realtime quota usage and called us.

irene: can you paste the wire trace? even partial.

ben: snippet (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
x-session-id: s_abc123
route-id: r-us-east-2a
...
-- stream chunk idx=0 prefix="Hello"
-- toolcall {"name":"db_fetch","ttl":30} -> proxy->nodeA
(client disconnect)
(reconnect to r-us-east-2b)
resume request: x-resume-offset: 42, x-session-id: s_abc123
nodeB sees expired toolcall TTL and issues toolcall again -> provisional charge B
```

jia: thanks. so root cause is split view of toolcall state across nodes + provisional billing happening at issue-time not finalization-time.

sam: can we avoid provisional charge for toolcalls until either: final ACK from model/runtime or a short grace window where only one node is allowed to claim charge?

irene: that risks undercounting when nodeA actually executed the toolcall and can never confirm. The runtime currently uses provisional semantics so we can surface early costs.

ben: telemetry perspective: we need consistent (route_id, session_id, resume_offset, toolcall_id, provisional_id) in traces so ledger can dedupe on reconciliation. Also surface an end-state flag: `toolcall_finalized:true|false`.

sam: agree. add two more fields: `resume_epoch` (incremented each reconnect) and `toolcall_owner_node`. Then reconciliation can pick the earliest successful owner.

jia: console UX change request: show an interactive timeline for streaming sessions: event rows for chunks, toolcalls, reconnects, provisional charges, and finalization. Right now console only shows aggregate tokens per minute which is confusing.

irene: small callout: routing policy makes this worse when we prefer lowest-latency node. Maybe change sticky routing to prefer session affinity for the first 60s to reduce cross-node handoffs for active streams.

ben: temporary mitigation: increase toolcall TTL propagation + per-session affinity, and switch provisional charging to include a `provisional_owner_node` tag so backend can auto-dedupe sooner.

ops-bot: deploy queued: infra/route-affinity-flag v2 -> canary 5% at 4399001800 by deploy-bot

sam: for billing team: we should also expose a `reconciliation_id` in billing export so ops can filter these reconcilations.

jia: implementation notes: we need change in three components: router (affinity + resume_epoch), runtime (emit toolcall_owner & finalized flag), ledger (dedupe logic on reconciliation_id or (session_id,resume_epoch,toolcall_id)).

ben: timeline? can we get a patch for canary by EOD?

irene: I can PR router + telemetry today, runtime needs a small change — will try tomorrow morning. Ledger changes need finance sign-off but I can draft design.

sam: also add an alert: when provisional charges for a single session exceed 200% of final charges in 10m window, auto-open an ops ticket.

ben: thanks — I'll follow up with a short doc and add example log lines for the ledger team.

jen (from billing, not in participants): @ben can you CC billing when you publish the doc? we want to see the reconciliation_id mapping.

ben: will do. :thumbsup:

(threads ends)
